skill.name: grasshopper-workflow
skill.description: Automates Rhino Grasshopper workflows through MCP. It helps create components, connect them, set parameters, and generate placement workflows from MMD planning files.
skill.summary: Build and execute repeatable Rhino Grasshopper workflows through MCP automation.
skill.author: AmemiyaLai

security_audit.summary: Most system-reconnaissance, external-command, and obfuscation alerts are false positives from component IDs, Markdown code fences, and Chinese or GUID-heavy documentation. I confirmed filesystem write risks where CLI and utility functions write or overwrite caller-selected JSON paths without path allowlisting or overwrite confirmation. No evidence of prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or concealed payloads was found.

remediation.issue: Caller-selected output paths can overwrite local files.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict generated outputs to a project workspace and require confirmation before overwriting existing files.

remediation.issue: In-place GUID updates modify the selected JSON file directly.
remediation.suggestion: Write updates to a new file by default or create a backup before saving changes.

remediation.issue: Default generated files are written relative to the package directory.
remediation.suggestion: Resolve paths with pathlib, document the location, and reject paths outside the active workspace.

content.value_statement: Building Rhino Grasshopper definitions from planning files can be slow and error-prone. This skill guides component planning, placement creation, and MCP execution for repeatable parametric workflows.
actual_capabilities: Creates Grasshopper components through a local MCP client.
Connects components using saved component ID mappings.
Sets Number Slider and Vector XYZ parameters.
Parses MMD planning files into component and connection data.
Generates placement workflow files for repeatable execution.
Groups related Grasshopper components with names and colors.
limitations: Requires a running Grasshopper MCP server on the configured host and port.
Writes workflow outputs and component ID maps to local files.
Does not verify final geometry quality inside Rhino.
Depends on supported component names, GUID mappings, and MMD formats.

use_cases.title: Create a Parametric Prototype
use_cases.description: Turn a simple design brief into component planning files and an executable Grasshopper workflow.

use_cases.title: Standardize Grasshopper Automation
use_cases.description: Use consistent MCP commands for component creation, connections, parameter setup, and grouping.

use_cases.title: Teach Workflow Structure
use_cases.description: Show students how design requirements map to MMD diagrams, placement steps, and Grasshopper components.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Simple Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan a simple Grasshopper model. Ask for missing dimensions, then outline the needed components and parameters.

prompt_templates.title: Create MMD Files
prompt_templates.prompt: Create part and component planning steps for this object. Use clear component names, parameters, and connection intent.

prompt_templates.title: Generate Placement Steps
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare execution from an existing component plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my component plan and prepare a placement workflow. Include component creation order, connections, slider values, and groups.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Full Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect this Grasshopper workflow plan for missing inputs, wrong GUIDs, unsafe paths, and execution risks before running MCP commands.

output_examples.input: A table with a rectangular top and four cylindrical legs.
output: A part breakdown for the tabletop and repeated leg geometry.
A component plan with sliders, planes, surfaces, extrusions, moves, and union steps.
A placement execution outline with creation, connection, parameter, and grouping phases.

output_examples.input: An existing component diagram has unresolved slider values.
output: A list of missing or ambiguous parameter values.
Suggested ranges for width, length, height, radius, and position sliders.
A reminder to review generated files before MCP execution.

output_examples.input: A placement workflow fails during connection creation.
output: A focused diagnosis of missing component IDs and mismatched parameter names.
A corrected connection plan using saved component ID mappings.
Next checks for Grasshopper document errors.

best_practices: Review generated MMD and placement files before running MCP execution.
Keep workflow outputs inside a dedicated project workspace.
Confirm component GUIDs against the active Grasshopper installation.
anti_patterns: Do not run generated placement files without checking paths and commands.
Do not assume every Grasshopper component name maps to the expected GUID.
Do not overwrite project files without keeping a reviewed backup.

faq.question: Does this skill require Rhino and Grasshopper?
faq.answer: Yes. It needs a local Grasshopper MCP server to execute component and parameter commands.

faq.question: Can it create a complete Grasshopper definition?
faq.answer: It can create components, connect them, set parameters, and group them when the plan is complete.

faq.question: Does it generate files?
faq.answer: Yes. It can generate planning files, placement workflows, and component ID map files.

faq.question: Is it limited to table examples?
faq.answer: No. The documentation includes table examples, but the workflow can support other planned parametric models.

faq.question: Can it validate geometry quality?
faq.answer: No. Users should inspect the final Rhino and Grasshopper result after execution.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
